meanings.note: In estar bien or estar mal, evaluates an action or situation.
Also links tratar de + infinitive and forms more than with más de; these uses do not express possession.

examples.trans: I've been here for more than two years.

examples.text: Te llamo la semana que viene.
Yo le enseñé a moverse en este mundillo.

meanings.note: Identity, profession or a characteristic; compare estar for a state or location.
Possession, relationships and many fixed expressions.
Tener algo claro means to understand it or have a firm view of it.

examples.text: Tiene muy claro lo que quiere.
examples.trans: She is very clear about what she wants.

examples.text: Tiene un gran tempo para la comedia.

examples.trans: Pay close attention to the pace of the scene.

examples.text: Es buena en drama y es buena en comedia.
examples.trans: She is good at drama and she is good at comedy.

examples.text: A ver, de verdad, niño, mira, ¿tú sabes cómo funciona esto?

meanings.note: Introduces a role or a comparison. No written accent in this use; the question word cómo is different.

meanings.note: The choice after experto is en; English may use at, in or on according to the following activity or subject.

meanings.note: Before a noun it is a determiner; standing alone, todos/todas can mean everyone or all of them.
